items.q: How did Eileen go from layoff to Head of AI in a year?
items.a: Laid off at **39** after 15 years as an email developer, she learned **n8n and Claude Code** via Nate's AIS community, **built in public**, and landed Head of AI at Yang (15 vertical brands) by answering with **video proof**, not resume claims.

items.q: Do you need a "real" CS background?
items.a: No. Her background was **email HTML/CSS**, not traditional engineering. Claude Code **"looks technical but is absolutely non-technical"** for builders willing to practice.

items.q: What learning sequence worked for her?
items.a: **Zapier → Make → n8n → Claude Code**. Use n8n with ChatGPT side-by-side for node-by-node builds; start from domain work: "every day I do X — **how can AI help?**"

items.q: How did she find practice time with a life and day job?
items.a: A structured **4 a.m. learning block** before family and work interruptions. Outsource paths and research to AI, but **never outsource understanding** of trade-offs.
HR's question: **"What have you built?"** Video demos, two YouTube channels, and LinkedIn separated her from ChatGPT cover letters. Views don't matter — **links and your face** do.

items.q: What did Hormozi's advice look like in practice?
items.a: **Show yourself** before you're ready. Her terrified first n8n meetup talk (**90+ people**) became LinkedIn proof and interview leverage. She applied to ~**10 targeted roles**, skipped HR to the CEO with demos, then completed a **two-week strategic trial**.

sections.title: What Head of AI actually means

items.q: Is Head of AI a pure executive seat?
items.a: No — it blends **strategy + hands-on builds + hiring**. Map processes per brand, decide what to automate vs keep human, build with Claude Code, hire from pipelines like AIS Plus. **If you're not hands-on every day, you're out.**

items.q: What market gap does the role close?
items.a: IBM survey frame: **76% of CEOs** now have a chief-AI-officer equivalent (up from 26%), while ~**85% of employees could use AI** but only ~**25% do**. Culture shift: remove **boring repetitive work**, not whole jobs.
